message_1_subject: Medisphere deep-dive: latency & throughput SLOs, model fit, topology
message_1_body:
Thanks again for the call earlier today — appreciate the detailed walk-through of your inference needs. Summarizing what we captured and the proposed next steps so we have an aligned action plan.

Key pain points you called out:
- User-facing conversational latency spikes during peak hours (90th/95th p95s hit ~700–900ms for short responses).
- Cost pressure on embedding workloads (batch embedding jobs for search with large throughput).
- Need for predictable tail latency for interactive features (SLOs tied to customer SLAs).
- Data residency and audit-log retention requirements for PII-sensitive transcripts.

Goals / success criteria for a POC:
- Demonstrate 95th percentile token-generation latency <= 400ms for baseline chat use case (avg response ~40 tokens).
- Support sustained embedding throughput of ~12k requests/hour with batching and caching without >10% degradation in latency SLOs.
- Show model parity on key prompts (we'll run the evaluation prompt set you shared).
- Provide a deployment topology that meets your VPC/KMS constraints and produces audit logs to your SIEM.

Technical notes (from our call):
- Primary model family: open Llama-2 style variants (you specified a 13B baseline); willingness to evaluate 7B quantized for cost-sensitive routes.
- KV cache warm-up was called out as a key source of early-request tail latency.
- Expected traffic pattern: steady daytime baseline (~2k req/hr) with two 1.5–2 hour peaks (~6–8k req/hr).

Attachments I’m sharing with this recap: medisphere_slo_matrix.xlsx (proposed SLOs & test cases), inference_topology_sketch.png (initial topology sketch), redwood_latency_profile.pdf (sample latency percentiles from similar deployments).

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) You share the evaluation prompt set + a small sample of production request traces (anonymized) — Alex, can you confirm ETA? (requested by 8/14)
2) Redwood to prepare a POC scoping doc with concrete SLO tests and an ops runbook (target 8/16).
3) Technical POC kickoff: 2-week slot beginning 8/24 — confirm if that aligns with your team.
4) Procurement: draft MPA and minimum capacity estimates for Dedicated/Private (we’ll loop procurement after acceptance of the POC scope).

If any of this is off from your interpretation, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll treat this as the agreed starting point and I’ll circulate the formal scoping doc by Monday.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: medisphere_slo_matrix.xlsx, inference_topology_sketch.png, redwood_latency_profile.pdf

message_3_body:
Drafting a compact technical approach for the scoping doc — sharing my notes so we can align before Neha sends the formal doc.

High-level topology options (trade-offs):
1) Hosted + Variant Routing (fastest to spin up)
   - Use Redwood Hosted with two pinned model variants: 13B (quantized 16-bit where possible) for SLA routes; 7B int8 for low-cost fallbacks.
   - Smart routing by policy: route to 13B if predicted response length > 60 tokens or if request flagged as high-priority (auth header / SLA token).
   - Pros: minimal ops, quick POC. Cons: data egress/residency considerations (can be mitigated with VPC peering + IP allowlist).

2) Dedicated Pool in customer VPC (middle ground)
   - Reserved GPU pool inside customer VPC with KMS integration for encryption-at-rest, audit logs forwarded to your SIEM.
   - Autoscale to handle 8k/hr peak; use batching window (20–30ms) for embeddings to hit throughput without violating latency SLO for chat by separating routes.
   - Pros: predictable performance, control over logs. Cons: onboarding time, capacity commit.

3) Private on-prem (if procurement pushes back)
   - Full private control, longer lead time, highest integration effort.

KV cache / warm-up mitigation:
- Implement prefix caching + proactive KV warming on session start for returning users (session affinity).
- Pre-warm hot KV keys during peak ramp-up windows; instrument to measure cold-start tail.

Quantization & perf knobs:
- Recommend an int8 path for 7B fallback. For 13B evaluate Q4_0 and FP16 to balance quality.
- Continuous batching for tokens with three queues: interactive chat, embeddings, background tasks.

POC test plan (short):
- Controlled load tests for 2k, 6k, 8k req/hr with representative token-length distributions.
- Latency SLA verification: p50/p95/p99 for 40-token and 150-token buckets.
- Model-quality check: run the evaluation prompt set (customer-provided) and compare top-line accuracy/fluency metrics.

Action items for the scoping doc:
- Include a configuration matrix that maps traffic shape -> recommended topology -> cost/order of magnitude.
- Prepare dashboards and tracing hooks we’ll surface during POC.

Flagging two questions for the external thread: energy around session affinity / how many unique users per hour (Alex provided request volumes but not unique sessions). Also need confirmation on whether embeddings can be batched asynchronously without strict latency SLO.

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
